raw_response:
I only have 1.5 mu, so I cannot take big risks. I am old now, and some people in the family work outside, so for maize I want a simple way that I know well and can manage without spending too much cash at once. In our place, if the land moisture is all right, I will plant in mid-late April. I will still use hybrid seed from the market, because saved seed does not give as even a stand and my neighbors who plant hybrid maize usually harvest better. Fertilizer, I will not calculate too finely. I will put most of it before or at planting, then look at the maize when it gets taller. If the leaves are a bit pale, I will add another round of urea. I have a well, so if spring is dry I will water after sowing, and then water again around jointing or tasseling if there is no good rain. For pests and weeds, I do not spray many times unless I see a real problem. I mostly want the field clean early and keep the maize growing steadily. With such a small plot, family labor is enough, so I do not plan to hire people.
